why:
Two Edits with identical EditInfo except that one side OMITS ThreeD and the other states FALSE are the same edit and must auto-match. Booleans default to false when unstated (common.xsd), so a mirror record that omits ThreeD is not 'different' from a sheet record that says no.

THE TRAP this pins: the naive comparison key -- read the attribute as-is, null on one side, false on the other -- reports `EditInfo differs (3D)`, sets the candidate to Reject, and through decisive_nomatch closes the row as `Disagree: all candidates rejected` WITHOUT review. That is the fail-CLOSED direction on a pair that is identical: the reviewer never sees the row, and the correct record is refused. The rule landed in BMR-Review's Python on 2026-09-11 but was pinned in one engine's unit test only; a JavaScript port built from a spec that said 'booleans pass through untouched' reproduces the closed failure exactly (De-Dupe UI, 2026-09-12).

Mutation-tested: reverting `_edit_key`'s ThreeD line to the raw `getattr(rec, 'three_d', None)` fails this fixture and no other.

SCOPE: pins that ABSENT compares equal to FALSE. It says nothing about whether ThreeD is compared at all -- `edit-three-d-true-vs-false-rejects` pins that, and the two are read together (specs/golden-pairs.md section 6, rule 2). No Alt ID on either side, so the pair cannot floor to Review through Guard 7 for a different reason.
